title: Data visualization
text:
Data visualization

Now that we have the results of our study, we should visualise it to disseminate the information.
In base R, we use plot() (and other functions) to draw figures.
In tidyverse, we use the ggplot2 package

title: Data visualization
text:
Example


Base R:

plot(
  x = mtcars$wt,
  y = mtcars$mpg,
  xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
  ylab = "Miles Per Gallon",
  main = "MPG vs. Weight",
  pch = 19,       # Solid circle points
  col = "blue"
)









ggplot2:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  scale_x_continuous("Weight (1000 lbs)") +
  scale_y_continuous("Miles Per Gallon") +
  ggtitle("MPG vs. Weight") + 
  theme_bw()

title: Data visualization
text:
ggplot2 structure

ggplot2 works directly with tidy data (same as everything under tidyverse).
It is based on a concept called “grammar of graphics”.
Has intuitive and comprehensive documentation on how to use it effectively.
Provide enough flexibility for customisation.

title: Data visualization
text:
Grammar of graphics

A framework to describe and construct graphics in a structured manner.
Has a layered approach, i.e. each component of a figure is a separate layer.

title: Data visualization
text:
Practice

set.seed(123)
np <- 50
rd <- data.frame(
  country = rep("", np),
  coverage = rnorm(n = np, mean = 0.1, sd = 0.12),
  inequality = rnorm(n = np, mean = -0.05, sd = 0.04),
  size = rnorm(n = np, mean = 1, sd = 0.4),
  color = sample(
    c("red", "green", "darkblue", "yellow", "blue", "purple"),
    np,
    replace = T
  )
)
head(rd)

  country   coverage   inequality      size color
1         0.03274292 -0.039867259 0.7158374 green
2         0.07237870 -0.051141870 1.1027535 green
3         0.28704500 -0.051714818 0.9013232   red
4         0.10846101  0.004744091 0.8609830 green
5         0.11551453 -0.059030839 0.6193526   red
6         0.30580780  0.010658824 0.9819889  blue



set.seed(123): dùng để cố định cách tạo ra các điểm ngẫu nhiên.
np <- 50: tạo ra 50 điểm ngẫu nhiên.
country = rep("", np): các điểm này không có tên quốc gia.
coverage = rnorm(n = np, mean = 0.1, sd = 0.12): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là 0.1 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.12.
inequality = rnorm(n = np, mean = -0.05, sd = 0.04): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là -0.05 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.04.
size = rnorm(n = np, mean = 1, sd = 0.4): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là 1 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.4.
color = sample(1:6, np, replace = T): màu sắc là số nguyên ngẫu nhiên từ 1 đến 6.

title: Overview of R
text:
What is R?

R is a programming language developed by Professor Robert Gentleman and Professor Ross Ihaka at the University of Auckland1. The name R is derived from the first letters of the two authors’ names (Robert and Ross).
For statistical computation and data visualization.
Includes a basic part (built-in when installing R) and extensions through packages

title: Overview of R
text:
Programming language

A programming language is a set of instructions that tell a computer to perform certain tasks.
Users communicate and converse with computers by entering sentences (code) like chatting with the computer, so that the computer understands and does exactly what the person wants.

title: Overview of R
text:
Using R because

Free, constantly updated.
Great for statistics and graphics.
Easy to store commands and re-execute.
Should use RStudio instead of basic R.
Completely self-taught from internet sources.

title: Overview of R
text:
Data analysis and visualization

R provides many powerful libraries like ggplot2, dplyr, tidyverse for data processing and visualization.
Commonly used in scientific, economic, medical and business research to analyze data and generate reports.

title: Overview of R
text:
Statistics and hypothesis testing

Supports statistical methods such as linear regression, t-test, ANOVA, and many other statistical models.
Suitable for academic research and in-depth data analysis.

title: Overview of R
text:
Machine Learning

There are libraries like caret, randomForest, e1071, xgboost for building predictive models.
R is commonly used to develop and evaluate machine learning models.

title: Overview of R
text:
Big Data Analytics

R can integrate with Apache Spark through sparklyr, which helps in big data processing.
Combining SQL, NoSQL for large-scale data analysis.

title: Overview of R
text:
Data science and automated reporting

R supports dynamic reporting with R Markdown, which helps automate data reporting.
R Shiny allows building interactive web applications to present data.

title: Overview of R
text:
Medicine and Biology

Supporting epidemiological research and disease modeling

title: Overview of R
text:
Git 

Git is an open source, version control system (VCS) whose purpose is to track changes to files in a repository and provide the ability to roll back to previous versions (including changes in open source code for computational models and algorithms over time).
Git is a local software. You do not need GitHub for Git to work. You can use Git independently.

title: Overview of R
text:
GitHub

GitHub is a cloud-based service for hosting Git.
Acts as a remote server for Git.
Web-based interface, free and public.

title: Overview of R
text:
Repository
Contains a collection of files and folders, records the history of changes, tracks their status and versions. There are two types:

Remote repository: Stored on a remote server, shared among multiple team members.
Local repository: Stored on a user’s personal computer.

title: Overview of R
text:
GitHub Desktop 

GitHub Desktop is a software that makes it easier for you to use Git. It is a software built by GitHub, again, separate from Git.
Advantages:

Keeps things simple and only provides commonly used Git functionality.
Reduces the chance of you making mistakes when using Git.
Integrates directly with GitHub, making authentication easier.

title: SWAPER
text:
Hello newbies,
Firstly, thank you for joining us in the department. The Department of Surveillance, Warning, and Preparedness for Epidemic Response (SWAPER) was established on June 1st, 2023. Our mission is to monitor and forecast epidemic trends, assess risks, and issue timely alerts. The department coordinates response efforts across all administrative levels, improves the quality of disease surveillance and early warning systems, and manages Ho Chi Minh City’s Emergency Operations Centre.
To fulfill this mission, we need to learn how to use R.
In this course, you’ll learn how to use R at a basic level. R is not just software — it is a programming language designed for data analysis and visualization. In public health, R allows us to analyze surveillance data, detect unusual patterns, and generate automatic reports and alerts. These tools strengthen our capacity to provide faster, data-driven responses to health threats.
Let’s get started. 🚀
Welcome home! 🏡
To more information about SWAPER, please click on following link:
https://hcdc-gscb.github.io/swaper/

title: Overview of R
text:
What is R?

R is a programming language developed by Professor Robert Gentleman and Professor Ross Ihaka at the University of Auckland1. The name R is derived from the first letters of the two authors’ names (Robert and Ross).
For statistical computation and data visualization.
Includes a basic part (built-in when installing R) and extensions through packages

title: Overview of R
text:
Programming language

A programming language is a set of instructions that tell a computer to perform certain tasks.
Users communicate and converse with computers by entering sentences (code) like chatting with the computer, so that the computer understands and does exactly what the person wants.

title: Overview of R
text:
Using R because

Free, constantly updated.
Great for statistics and graphics.
Easy to store commands and re-execute.
Should use RStudio instead of basic R.
Completely self-taught from internet sources.

title: Overview of R
text:
Installation R
R Official Website: https://www.r-project.org

title: Overview of R
text:
Installation R-Studio
RStudio Official Website: https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/
R must be installed before RStudio can be installed.

title: Overview of R
text:
Data analysis and visualization

R provides many powerful libraries like ggplot2, dplyr, tidyverse for data processing and visualization.
Commonly used in scientific, economic, medical and business research to analyze data and generate reports.

title: Overview of R
text:
Statistics and hypothesis testing

Supports statistical methods such as linear regression, t-test, ANOVA, and many other statistical models.
Suitable for academic research and in-depth data analysis.

title: Overview of R

title: Overview of R
text:
Git 

Git is an open source, version control system (VCS) whose purpose is to track changes to files in a repository and provide the ability to roll back to previous versions (including changes in open source code for computational models and algorithms over time).
Git is a local software. You do not need GitHub for Git to work. You can use Git independently.

title: Overview of R
text:
GitHub

GitHub is a cloud-based service for hosting Git.
Acts as a remote server for Git.
Web-based interface, free and public.

title: Overview of R
text:
Repository
Contains a collection of files and folders, records the history of changes, tracks their status and versions. There are two types:

Remote repository: Stored on a remote server, shared among multiple team members.
Local repository: Stored on a user’s personal computer.

title: Overview of R
text:
GitHub Desktop 

GitHub Desktop is a software that makes it easier for you to use Git. It is a software built by GitHub, again, separate from Git.
Advantages:

Keeps things simple and only provides commonly used Git functionality.
Reduces the chance of you making mistakes when using Git.
Integrates directly with GitHub, making authentication easier.

In base R, we use plot() (and other functions) to draw figures.
In tidyverse, we use the ggplot2 package

title: Data visualization
text:
ggplot2 structure

ggplot2 works directly with tidy data (same as everything under tidyverse).
It is based on a concept called “grammar of graphics”.
Has intuitive and comprehensive documentation on how to use it effectively.
Provide enough flexibility for customisation.

title: Data visualization
text:
Grammar of graphics

A framework to describe and construct graphics in a structured manner.
Has a layered approach, i.e. each component of a figure is a separate layer.

2         0.07237870 -0.051141870 1.1027535 green
3         0.28704500 -0.051714818 0.9013232   red

6         0.30580780  0.010658824 0.9819889  blue



set.seed(123): dùng để cố định cách tạo ra các điểm ngẫu nhiên.
np <- 50: tạo ra 50 điểm ngẫu nhiên.
country = rep("", np): các điểm này không có tên quốc gia.
coverage = rnorm(n = np, mean = 0.1, sd = 0.12): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là 0.1 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.12.
inequality = rnorm(n = np, mean = -0.05, sd = 0.04): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là -0.05 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.04.
size = rnorm(n = np, mean = 1, sd = 0.4): số thực được tạo ra ngẫu nhiên theo phân phối bình thường với trung bình là 1 và độ lệch chuẩn là 0.4.
color = sample(1:6, np, replace = T): màu sắc là số nguyên ngẫu nhiên từ 1 đến 6.
